\ No newline at end of file === DIFF: docs/learning/lessons/0040-streamlit-execution-model.html === @@ -0,0 +1,175 @@ + + + + + +0040 — Streamlit's Execution Model: Whole-Script Reruns and Where State Lives + + + +

HFT Practice · Lesson 0040

+

Streamlit's Execution Model: Whole-Script Reruns and Where State Lives

+
Why this matters: the platform now has a real +Streamlit app (streamlit_app/dashboard.py, PR #75). Streamlit's core +trick — rerun the ENTIRE script on every interaction — is what makes it feel +effortless, and it is also the thing that silently breaks apps whose authors +don't know where state is allowed to live.
+ +

1 · The model

+

Click a button, type in a box, switch a tab: Streamlit throws away the frame +and executes your script again from line 1. Widgets aren't event handlers — +they're functions that return their current value during this rerun. +st.button returns True exactly once (the rerun caused by the +click), then False on every later rerun. There is no callback soup and +no DOM to reconcile — but it means module-level variables reset on every +interaction, so anything that must SURVIVE a rerun needs an explicit home:

+ + + + + +
StateCorrect homeIn our console
Widget valuesThe widgets themselves (keyed by position/label)Sidebar paths, tickers, interval
Accumulated data across interactionsst.session_statetape_seen (signal dedupe), tape_lines (bounded scrollback)
Module globalsNowhere — reset every rerunDeliberately none
+
# dashboard.py — why the tape survives the rerun the button causes:
+seen = st.session_state.setdefault("tape_seen", {})
+lines = st.session_state.setdefault("tape_lines", [])
+if refresh:                      # True only on the click-rerun
+    lines.append(...)            # mutates the session_state object
+    st.session_state["tape_lines"] = lines[-200:]  # bounded scrollback
+ +

2 · The two guards this repo added

+

Import-safety guard. streamlit run executes the file +top-to-bottom, so apps put their build at module level — but our suite must be +able to import the module in an environment with NO streamlit. The fix pins the +launch to a real script-run context:

+
if __name__ == "__main__" or _in_streamlit_run():
+    main()
+# _in_streamlit_run(): streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner.get_script_run_ctx()
+# is not None — true under `streamlit run` AND under AppTest, false for
+# plain imports. Pinned by test_plain_import_never_launches_the_app.
+

Logic/presentation split. Reruns make UI code awkward to unit +test — so everything testable lives in streamlit_app/data.py (pure, no +streamlit import, read-only mode=ro SQLite), and the UI file is thin +enough that streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest can exercise it whole: run the +script, assert on at.metric/at.dataframe/at.exception.

+ +

3 · Often confused

+ + + + + +
PairDistinction
Rerun model vs callback model (Tkinter/FastAPI)gui_app.py wires callbacks to long-lived widgets; webapp routes handle one request each. Streamlit re-executes everything and RECONSTRUCTS widgets — state lives in session_state, not in the widget tree or module.
st.session_state vs @st.cache_datasession_state is per-browser-tab mutable memory; cache_data memoizes function results across reruns (and users) keyed by arguments. The tape's dedupe dict must NOT be cached — it's stateful, not a pure function result.
The lab web theme vs this consoleThe webapp's "lab" theme is FastAPI wearing Streamlit's CSS; this is actual Streamlit — reruns, session_state, AppTest and all. Two different programs that happen to share an aesthetic.
+ +

4 · Practice

+

Score: 0 / 0

+ +
+

Q1. A module-level tape_lines = [] in dashboard.py would appear to "work" briefly, then always show an empty tape. Why?

+
    +
  • Each interaction reruns the script, resetting the global to []
    • +
  • Streamlit runs each widget in its own thread
    • +
  • The GC collects lists without references
    • +
  • st.code can't display lists
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q2. Why does st.button("↻ Refresh") only fetch the tape once per click instead of on every subsequent rerun?

+
    +
  • Streamlit debounces buttons for 30 seconds
    • +
  • The button returns True only on the click-caused rerun
    • +
  • session_state suppresses repeat fetches
    • +
  • cache_data memoizes the fetch
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q3. The dashboard deliberately does NOT use ArenaState to read the arena DB. What's the reason?

+
    +
  • ArenaState is too slow for a dashboard
    • +
  • ArenaState's constructor migrates (writes); the console opens mode=ro instead
    • +
  • strategy_arena can't be imported without streamlit
    • +
  • compare_strategies requires a raw connection
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q4. Why do the AppTest console tests auto-skip in the core dev environment?

+
    +
  • They're too slow for CI
    • +
  • streamlit is an opt-in extra; importorskip enforces the streamlit-free core contract
    • +
  • AppTest needs a real browser
    • +
  • They only test mocks
    • +
+

+
+ + +
+ + Investigate per the method in your instructions, then return the findings list.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Looking at this change: two static HTML files for a learning documentation site — an index page update (lesson count + one new row) and a new lesson page with a client-side quiz. **Analysis:** 1. **docs/learning/index.html** — Only changes are text content (count from 11→12) and a new `
` link to the new lesson. No script changes, no data flow, no sinks. 2. **docs/learning/lessons/0040-streamlit-execution-model.html** — Static HTML with an embedded quiz. Reviewed the full file: - **No entry points**: No form submission, no fetch/XHR, no URL param reading, no `location.hash`/`search` usage, no `postMessage` handlers. - **All data is author-authored static content** baked into the HTML (`data-correct`, `data-why` attributes are literals in the source). - **Script sinks reviewed**: - `feedback.textContent = ...` — uses `textContent` (safe, not `innerHTML`), so even if `data-why` contained markup it would render as text. - `list.appendChild(li)` — reordering existing DOM nodes; no injection surface. - `Math.random()` for shuffle — cosmetic only, no security context. - `document.getElementById('score').textContent = ...` — number concatenation, safe. - No `eval`, no `new Function`, no `innerHTML`/`outerHTML`/`document.write`, no `href=javascript:`, no dynamic script/style injection. - No external resources loaded (no `
